acceptance.duplicate_gate: Versioned domain-tagged semantic-core key derived before writes; best-effort repository search must return zero matches. Duplicate means no event, no CURRENT update, no Slack.
acceptance.pointer_gate: Reject the stale semantic candidate before any write because expected_version and prior_digest do not match observed CURRENT even though it carries the current blob SHA. Then commit and read back this event; fetch CURRENT again; update only if version=39, projection digest=9dc3b803d1c76d0c0c6ec00199d8d0ebebe6598c7eeff25b67b8fbfe003a6b68, and blob=39c981827a4f620b04fe5864304b9db2e3930116; read back CURRENT, this event, and predecessor.
acceptance.slack_rule: Post once only after v40 advances and the C10 campaign decision is durable. The rejected stale semantic candidate receives no separate Slack post.
acceptance.stale_rule: A candidate presenting expected_version=38 and prior_digest=a74f7e964e45111cc224488bbc05a84fa7ecde4d8e9d1be77862901d2e7ba0dd is stale against observed v39/dd631725..., even though it copies the current file blob SHA. Reject before GitHub update_file; do not rely on file SHA alone for application semantics.

experiment.controlled_factor: Keep C10 event-first, duplicate, exact-read, and single-file blob-SHA gates fixed; vary only whether a stale writer can copy the current blob SHA while presenting stale application expected_version and prior_digest fields.
experiment.hypothesis: The X12 application gate rejects a semantically stale envelope before any Git write even when the envelope carries the currently observed CURRENT blob SHA. Git's single-file SHA precondition does not encode X12 expected_version or prior-event-digest semantics, so both gates remain necessary.
experiment.strongest_falsifier: The stale semantic candidate reaches update_file; a mismatch advances CURRENT; the proposed idempotency key already exists; exact second read changes before pointer update; event digest recomputation fails; final chain bindings disagree; or campaign facts do not support KEEP.

canonical_transition.honest_flaw: Wake 4 is an application-level preflight specimen, not an actual same-SHA GitHub rejection: no unsafe API update was attempted for the semantically stale envelope. Across C10, the four HTTP 409 observations were sequential stale-blob calls, not simultaneous writers. The campaign supports a bounded dual gate—application expected-version/prior-digest checks plus one-file blob-SHA replacement—not locks, fairness, linearizability, serializable isolation, cross-file atomicity, database durability, exactly-once execution, Slack atomicity, server-side idempotency uniqueness, referential integrity, or automatic orphan repair. Event creation, CURRENT replacement, validation reads, and Slack remain separate effects.
canonical_transition.rollback: Append a compensating event from the then-current version; never delete this event or Slack message; replace CURRENT only with its exact then-current blob SHA.
canonical_transition.transaction_time_evidence: AUTOMATION_RUNTIME_CLOCK+NATIVE_TASK_INVENTORY_READBACK+GITHUB_COMMIT_METADATA; application preflight is not a database transaction boundary
